The book is often divided by hunger, cold and poverty, and the servant does not feel any compassion for it. It is appropriate. The only wonder is that Jin Qing, as a noble son, suffered from this trouble but did not lose his integrity, and his poetry became more and more skillful, transcending the joy of the world. This is what Confucius called a person who can live with a long time and be happy for a long time. Written by Su Shi on the eighth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yuan You.　　Su Shi was 49 years old in the first year of Yuan You of the Northern Song Dynasty (1086).　　This post inserts "Jin Gong Bo Jing Jian Seal", "Jing Xing Wei Xian", "Xiao Ru An Secret Book", "Bian Ling Zhi Identification", etc. The collection seal is four-sided, and there are six half-prints such as "style ancient hall" on the left and right. The postscript is recorded in Dongpo ji (Collection of Dongpo), vol. 165. In the Dongpo Collection, Volume 13, there is also a record of another postscript of Su Shi, "and Wang Jinqing's poem, and narrative": "In the second year of Yuanfeng, I was deported to Huangzhou, and Wang Monk, the captain of the team of harnessed soldiers, was also relegated to a faraway place, and did not hear from each other for seven years. I was called to use, and inon also returned to the court, met outside the temple door, sighed, made a poem to belong to. The words are not carefully crafted, but the poem is a tribute to a poor but not resentful person, not proud of himself, and I pity his noble son for having such aspirations, so I rhymed with him."
